name: Question 15
problem:
Solve the initial value problem

$$
x\frac{dy}{dx}+(x+1)y=\frac{3}{xy},\,y(1)=\sqrt{3},\,x>0,\,y>0.
$$

*Hint: You may wish to make use of the fact that the given differential equation can be transformed into the equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+2z=6
$$

using the substitution $z={x}^{2}{y}^{2}.$*
worked_solution:
The substitution $z={x}^{2}{y}^{2}$ transforms the given equation into the equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+2z=6.
$$

The above equation is in the standard form

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+P(x)z=Q(x)
$$

with

$$
P(x)=2,\,Q(x)=6\,.
$$

We then compute an integrating factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(x) & ={e}^{\int P(x)\,\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{\int 2\,\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{2x}\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides of the equation in standard form by $I(x)={e}^{2x}$ yields

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{2x}\cdot (\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+2z) & ={e}^{2x}\cdot 6 \\ {e}^{2x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+2{e}^{2x}z & =6{e}^{2x} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{2x}z) & =6{e}^{2x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{2x}z)\,\text{d}x & =6\int {e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x \\ {e}^{2x}z & =3{e}^{2x}+C \\ z & =3+C{e}^{-2x}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we determine $y(x)$ by writing $z={x}^{2}{y}^{2}.$ This results in

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}{y}^{2} & =3+C{e}^{-2x} \\ {y}^{2} & =\frac{3+C{e}^{-2x}}{{x}^{2}} \\ y & =\frac{\sqrt{3+C{e}^{-2x}}}{x}\,,\end{aligned}
$$

where we used that $x>0$ and $y>0.$

From the initial condition $y(1)=\sqrt{3}$ we determine $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3} & =\frac{\sqrt{3+C{e}^{-2}}}{1}\,⟹\,C=0\end{aligned}
$$

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{x}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15
?

Solve the initial value problem xdydx+(x+1)y=3xy,y(1)=3,x>0,y>0.

Hint: You may wish to make use of the fact that the given differential equation can be transformed into the equation dzdx+2z=6 using the substitution z=x2y2.

a
y=3+e−2xx
b
y=3x
c
y=1+3exx
d
y=4−x3x
e
y=5−2x3x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The substitution z=x2y2 transforms the given equation into the equation dzdx+2z=6.

The above equation is in the standard form dzdx+P(x)z=Q(x)

with P(x)=2,Q(x)=6.

We then compute an integrating factor: I(x)=e∫P(x)dx=e∫2dx=e2x

Multiplying both sides of the equation in standard form by I(x)=e2x yields e2x⋅(dzdx+2z)=e2x⋅6e2x⋅dzdx+2e2xz=6e2xddx(e2xz)=6e2x.

Now, we integrate with respect to x: ∫ddx(e2xz)dx=6∫e2xdxe2xz=3e2x+Cz=3+Ce−2x

Next, we determine y(x) by writing z=x2y2. This results in

x2y2=3+Ce−2xy2=3+Ce−2xx2y=3+Ce−2xx, where we used that x>0 and y>0.

From the initial condition y(1)=3 we determine C: 3=3+Ce−21⟹C=0

So we have y=3x.
